function: Joint active (AP) and passive (IRS) beamforming for sum-rate maximization under phase shift noise, using a lightweight cascade CNN (LCCNN) trained without labels (pp. 1, 5).
system: IRS-assisted multiuser MISO: AP with M=2 to 8 antennas, reflecting IRS with N=4 to 48 elements, K single-antenna users, direct links blocked; carrier frequency not given (pp. 4, 10).
method: Lightweight cascade CNN (PassiveNet with depthwise separable convolutions, ActiveNet MLP); unsupervised one-stage training with a loss from the closed-form expected sum rate, no labels (pp. 6-8).
data_channel: Own simulator: indoor office, Rayleigh small-scale fading, path loss 20.4 log10(d), uniform phase shift noise; 160,000 training, 40,000 validation, 10,000 test samples; no standard or measured data (p. 8).
test_conditions: Sweeps over M and N, network sizes tied to M, N, K (pp. 7-10); one 8-user model tested on 2 to 8 users without retraining (p. 11).
baselines: Non-learned: BCD, SDR, SLSQP, L-BFGS-B, COBYLA, CG, random beamforming; learned: CNN of [15] and lightweight CNN without cascade, compared on training loss only (pp. 8-11).
metrics: Sum data rate (bits/s) versus N, M, and K; training loss; complexity orders and inference time in ms (pp. 9-11).
complexity: Table IV: O(K^2 M N^2) for LCCNN versus O(L K M N^2) for CNN [15]; Table V: inference 0.14 ms (M=2, N=16) and 0.21 ms (M=4, N=32) (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 8: "The wireless channels under consideration are subject to Rayleigh small-scale fading". Own simulator with path loss 20.4 log10(d/d_f) and an office layout (Fig. 3); no 3GPP, QuaDRiGa, COST 2100, DeepMIMO, or measured data is used.
q2_support: p. 11: "After training the Generalized LCCNN for the 8-user system, we evaluate its performance on systems with different numbers of users, ranging from 2 users to 8 users." Fig. 7 shows comparable rate without re-training.
q3_support: p. 8: "comparing the training loss with two benchmark models", the CNN of [15] and a lightweight CNN without cascade; Fig. 4 (p. 9) shows only training loss versus epochs. The data-rate comparison (Fig. 6, p. 10) is with BCD, standard optimizers, and random beamforming, none of them learned.
q4_support: p. 11: "The approximate complexity of various beamforming techniques for a single computation is summarized in Table IV". Table IV gives O(K^2 M N^2) for LCCNN; Table V gives inference times of 0.14 and 0.21 ms.
q5_support: p. 8: "The dataset comprises 160,000 training samples, 40,000 validation samples, and 10,000 test samples." The samples come from the authors' own simulator; no code or data link, DOI, public dataset, or measured data is given.
notes: Included, area 3: joint active and passive beamforming for an IRS-assisted multiuser MISO system with phase shift noise, learned without labels. Tables III to V (pp. 8, 11) and Figs. 4 and 6 (pp. 9, 10) were read from page images. q3 is borderline: the earlier learned baseline (CNN of [15]; the Fig. 4 legend cites [17]) and the lightweight CNN appear only as training loss versus epochs, and the loss adds an L2 penalty (p. 6); the abstract's (p. 1) "comparable data rates to parameter-intensive networks" has no data-rate figure behind it. If the reviewer accepts the training loss, the negative rate objective, as performance, q3 would be 1. q2: the Generalized and Specialized LCCNN of Fig. 7 are variants of the proposed method, not baselines.
